papers.Title: The "Echo State" Approach to Analysing and Training Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.Publication venue: GMD Report 148, German National Research Center for Information Technology
papers.Relevance rationale: Introduced echo state networks and the separation of a fixed recurrent reservoir from a trainable linear output layer, establishing the central classical reservoir-computing principle.

papers.Title: Real-Time Computing Without Stable States: A New Framework for Neural Computation Based on Perturbations
papers.Authors: Wolfgang Maass; Thomas Natschläger; Henry Markram
papers.Relevance rationale: Introduced liquid state machines, showing that a sufficiently rich fixed excitable dynamical system can provide real-time high-dimensional representations for task-specific readout.

papers.Title: Harnessing Disordered-Ensemble Quantum Dynamics for Machine Learning
papers.Relevance rationale: The foundational quantum reservoir-computing proposal; it used dissipative spin-network dynamics and showed that fixed quantum dynamics can create features for linear temporal tasks.

papers.Title: Quantum Reservoir Processing
papers.Authors: Sanjib Ghosh; Andrzej Opala; Michał Matuszewski; Tomasz Paterek; Timothy C. H. Liew
papers.Relevance rationale: Demonstrated quantum reservoir processing for pattern classification and related tasks, emphasizing that the reservoir can perform feature transformation while only the output layer is trained.

papers.Title: Boosting Computational Power through Spatial Multiplexing in Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.Authors: Kohei Nakajima; Keisuke Fujii; Makoto Negoro; Kazuaki Mitarai; Masahiro Kitagawa
papers.Relevance rationale: Introduced spatial multiplexing for quantum reservoirs and showed how combining multiple distinct quantum subsystems or input placements can improve memory and nonlinear processing.

papers.Title: Optimizing a Quantum Reservoir Computer for Time Series Prediction
papers.Authors: Aki Kutvonen; Keisuke Fujii; Takahiro Sagawa
papers.Relevance rationale: Examined design and parameter optimization for quantum reservoirs on time-series prediction tasks, including tradeoffs among system dynamics, memory, and prediction accuracy.

papers.Title: Temporal Information Processing on Noisy Quantum Computers
papers.Authors: Hsin-Yuan Chen; Hendra I. Nurdin; Naoki Yamamoto
papers.Relevance rationale: Developed a framework for temporal tasks on noisy gate-based quantum hardware and identified practical effects of finite measurements, noise, and device limitations.

papers.Title: Opportunities in Quantum Reservoir Computing and Extreme Learning Machines
papers.Authors: Pere Mujal; Rodrigo Martínez-Peña; Johannes Nokkala; Jorge García-Baldó; Roberta Zambrini; Miguel C. Soriano
papers.Relevance rationale: A major methodological and conceptual review connecting quantum reservoir computing with extreme learning machines, outlining experimental platforms, memory, scalability, readout, and noise limitations.

papers.Title: Gaussian States of Continuous-Variable Quantum Systems Provide Universal Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.Authors: Johannes Nokkala; Rodrigo Martínez-Peña; Gianluca Giorgi; Valentina Parigi; Miguel C. Soriano; Roberta Zambrini
papers.Relevance rationale: Established universality results for continuous-variable Gaussian reservoirs and showed how accessible observables and nonlinear features support a broad class of temporal transformations.

papers.Title: Higher-Order Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.Relevance rationale: Extended quantum reservoir representations through higher-order tensor products of reservoir observables, expanding nonlinear expressivity and temporal feature space.
